mis_merges.label: treasury long end intervention
subjects: US Treasury's Twist-style operation to cap long-end yields
Fed repo facility lending to Japan to support a sliding yen
mis_merges.why: These are unrelated stories (US debt-management policy vs. an emergency FX/BoJ-adjacent intervention) that a pulse editor would run as separate themes, and bundling them risks the yen-repo fact — a genuinely notable, under-covered story — being lost inside a Treasury-buyback write-up.

mis_merges.label: commodities debasement
subjects: Iran/oil geopolitical escalation pushing Brent toward $100
mis_merges.why: The stray Iran/oil line is one card of five and that story is already prominent and well-covered under the separate Hormuz/oil cluster, so no theme would be missed.

mis_merges.label: non us central bank previews
mis_merges.why: Hungary and Turkey are single-card, peripheral previews that would never have been standalone themes, and the ECB portion duplicates content already carrying its own well-populated label cluster.

notes: Fragmentation is pervasive and systemic: nearly every major bank research note in this ledger (JPM's weekly positioning note, JPM's International MI desk note, GS's Rothera/HOOD deep dive, JPM's Taiwan packaging tech-tour, the Fed/CPI/jobs complex, Hormuz oil coverage) was split across 3-7 near-duplicate labels, often with verbatim-repeated sentences. The 20 clusters listed are a documented lower bound from the labels actually cross-checked; the true fragmented share is likely higher given hundreds of remaining labels not individually traced.
